text:
alex: :rotating_light: Seeing sustained GPU pressure in eu-2-pool for last 8m, queue depth up x4 and preemptions spiking. Telemetry shows two noisy tenants responsible for ~55% of active requests. Can we do an emergency softcap / per-customer throttle?
nina: On it. Do we want global rate-limit or per-customer softcap? my vote: softcap top noisy customers first to avoid broad impact.
zach: Agree with targeting. Can you paste the customer IDs? I can push policy via admin tools.
alex: IDs: cust_1029, cust_4312, cust_7701. Pattern: long-lived streaming sessions + large batch embed requests. Sample metric: `eu2_gpu_util=98%`, `inflight=1280`, `avg_latency_tokens=420ms`.
ops-bot: [ALERT] region eu2 - GPU util 98% (5m), preemptions 23/min, backlog increasing. Recommend mitigation: per-customer softcap or traffic shift.
maya: Heads up: cust_4312 is on a paid Dedicated plan. We should confirm SLA impact before throttling. I'll ping their account owner.
nina: Good catch. For Dedicated customers we should prefer fallback to other regions or graceful limits. For hosted customers apply 60% throttle on model-infer tokens. Proposed policy snippet:
```
policy: softcap
region: eu2
targets:
  - cust_1029: max_qps: 8
  - cust_4312: max_qps: 12 (notify, skip hard-cut)
  - cust_7701: max_qps: 6
fallback: route_to_region: us-east-1 (best-effort)
```
I will apply with dry-run then enforce.
azch: small typo in your name :)
alex: heh :) nina apply when ready, tag me. Also kick off quick migration to us-east for non-Dedicated traffic.
nina: Running admin command now:
```
rdwctl quota apply --region eu2 --policy softcap --file /tmp/eu2-softcap-185123.json --enforce=false
```
Applying dry-run..
deploy-bot: Command accepted. Dry-run results: would throttle cust_1029 (est reduction 48% requests), cust_4312 (25%), cust_7701 (52%). No SLA violation flagged for hosted tiers.
nina: Dry-run looks safe. Enforcing in 2m: `--enforce=true` unless objections.
maya: I confirmed cust_4312 account owner; they request a heads-up and prefer failover rather than immediate throttling. Can we route their traffic to us-west instead of hard throttle?
alex: Yes, for cust_4312 do region failover. Update policy: route cust_4312 to us-west-1.
nina: Updating... applying enforcement now.
```
rdwctl quota apply --region eu2 --policy softcap --file /tmp/eu2-softcap-185123.json --enforce=true
```
deploy-bot: Enforcement complete. Policy ID: pol_202604_apr_eu2_07. Affected sessions: 1,214.
ops-bot: [METRICS] 60s after enforcement: eu2_gpu_util=73%, inflight=610, avg_latency_tokens=210ms, preemptions 3/min. Backlog decreasing.
zach: Great. Kicking off background shift for non-Dedicated traffic to us-east and us-west to reduce risk. `traffic-shift start --from eu2 --to us-east,us-west --filter tier!=dedicated`
deploy-bot: Traffic shift job started: job_885. Estimated 12m to complete gradual migration.
maya: I'll coordinate comms with cust_4312 customers and let them know we routed them to us-west.
alex: Thanks team. Follow-ups: nina please update runbook with softcap play and policy id; zach add a temporary dashboard for per-customer throttles; maya note CS messages. After shift completes we'll review for permanent capacity or quota adjustments. :thumbsup:
